run_card.hypothesis: D8 drainage-network topology on the 100 m DEM — aligned channel knickpoints (downstream jumps in normalised steepness k_sn = slope * A^0.45) and flow-azimuth deflections across adjacent ephemeral washes — traces oblique/strike-slip and sheetwash-eroded piedmont faults whose interfluve scarps have been erased and that surface mapping and local-filter geomorphology miss. Seven label-free drainage channels (log flow accumulation, k_sn, knickpoint jump, knickpoint co-linearity lineament, channel distance, HAND, azimuth bend) added to the 52-channel DPRF1 stitched-OOF stack — and gating its concealed Regime-B allocation — recover held-out whole fault segments better than the identical pipeline without them.
run_card.mechanism: D8 steepest-descent routing (O'Callaghan & Mark 1984) on the Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 2 px) DEM with no depression filling (endorheic sinks terminate accumulation; sink census recorded in drainage_diagnostics) yields exact upslope area A by descending-elevation propagation. Stream-power steepness k_sn = S * A^0.45 (Flint 1974; Wobus et al. 2006) jumps downstream where a wash crosses an uplifting or laterally offset fault block; co-linear jumps across >=3 neighbouring washes and systematic azimuth bends localise the buried trace even where the scarp itself is gone. Supervised stitched-OOF, stratified near+far negatives, selective residualization (drainage channels protected as terrain), relief calibration, ridge sharpening, apron debiasing and the two-regime 300 m submodular allocator are reused unchanged from DPRF1, isolating the drainage increment.
run_card.named_non_fault_mimic: Resistant lithologic hogbacks (welded ash-flow tuff or dike ribs) producing lithologic knickpoints across parallel gullies, alluvial fan-lobe avulsion channels, Pleistocene Lake Lahontan recessional strandlines, and road borrow ditches — all of which bend or steepen ephemeral washes without any Quaternary faulting or geothermal upflow.
